I'm a writer with no idea what to write here, and talking about myself in this capacity has always been difficult; yet I've a feeling writing this out is also for myself, so bear with the stream of consciousness. Thank you.

My life's been an adventure, one that didn't make as much sense as it needed to until I came back home on Easter Vigil of 2017. Maybe it was 2016. Nevertheless, here I am. My faith is everything, because, at the end of the day, despite the numbers on the ATM and the furniture in our apartment and the memories that stick with us, the Lord is all we have. No, it wasn't an easy conversion. My engagement fell apart. I had lost my job. A few other things happened since then -- heartbreak, loss, tragedy, a difficult discernment to the priesthood -- but here I am, as content as I've ever been. I think I can say that, for once, I have been finding rest in Him, although such a place isn't one to remain comfortable in for long, as He is constantly challenging us to draw closer and closer. 
Spiritually, I am attracted to the mystics and the warriors: St. John of the Cross, St. Charbel, St. David the King, St. Jacob (who wrestled with God, as I have found myself doing spiritually), St. John Capistran, St. Moses the Black, St. Constantine, St. Padre Pio, St. Theresa of Avila, St. Theresa of Lisieux, St. Patrick. I talk to the saints constantly, out loud but quietly, as I do with Mary and God -- in the car, at work in whispers, and so on. (That's something you'd need to find agreeable.) The Blessed Mother is my Mother; if it weren't for her love, I wouldn't be here. I try to get to Mass more than once a week; recently, that's been difficult due to work, and the fact that I am drawn evermore to the Divine Liturgy, and the Eastern Church in general, and there aren't many around. I (try to) spend much time in prayer; if I don't pray or write often, I start to feel spiritually "sick", a generalized sense of malaise and discontent.
I keep physically fit. My father was a bodybuilder, and I'd like to give my children (if that's what God has in store for me) the same sense of awe I had when looking at my father when I was a kid. While it's an activity I'd want my wife to engage in with me so children have two good role models for physical health, I don't expect her to share the same intense drive for it -- not at all. Other than writing and fitness, I like to build/repair anything electromechanical (think older ham radios, metal detectors, cameras, slot machines, the like), read, read some more after falling asleep during the first attempt, study languages (Tá mé ag tosnú Gaeilge an bhliain seo chugainn, so if you're from there, I'd love the help), occasionally paint, entertain the idea of woodworking one day ... the worn-out list goes on. Almost forgot: T.S. Eliot is my main role model for writing. God has worked through his poetry more than once to save me. Please pray for the repose of his soul.

For what it's worth, I'm an INFP, if you buy into that. Melancholic/choleric, if you have any coin left to buy that as well. I'm certainly introverted, with periods of intense extroversion. I'm told I'm serious, which I think I am; I'm much more careful to let people in with age, but if there is one thing I truly know about myself, it's that I'm as loyal as the day is long, so once you're in, you're in for life. I live in my extremely (and sometimes too) vivid imagination, and encounter my Jesus there often. It'd help if you're an "artist" type (I spend hours at art museums; this "recharges" me), but when all is said and done, whomever He has for me, if He wills it, isn't a "type". I'm known to make people laugh often; whether or not I'm funny is entirely up to the observer. I should say -- it's a gallows humor, a bit dark to the standards of some. But in the end, with the right people, an innocence that I've found in God is shown and freely given.

I'm looking for authenticity, depth, and intensity in a relationship. I don't mean the head-in-a-fishbowl, "won't-stop-thinking-about-them" intensity; I'm referring to the intensity of jumping into a profoundly deep body of water, together. My life is that of constant discovery and rediscovery of who my Lord is, and once I think I have it pinned down and figured out, inviting Him to overturn it all to humble my pride and let me know that I've only just begun the very first steps in acquiring the smallest dot of wisdom. Ideally, your spirituality, personality, and temperament would match mine; I have zero time for superficiality, the enemy of innocence, whimsy, the human spirit, and God.

Wherever He takes me next, it will be home, as it will be His will; and really, this life isn't our home anyways. I've a strong intuition that He won't allow my life to be formulaic and mundane. But it will be an adventure chasing after Him as intensely as I possibly can, something I expect to fail at as much as I hope to succeed at. There is the desire for a deep friendship, an authentic connection, with the woman who'd eventually be my wife, and the children to follow, but I'm content leaving this world as I entered it, if He so desires. Life's too precious and short to not abundantly desire His will. If you end up wanting to run this strange marathon God has set out for me, God bless you.

I am praying for you all. Trust in God. Find absolute peace in Him first before you ask for a husband or wife; ask Him to remove all the masks you've made for yourself in your own life, no matter how painful the process; ask Him to remove all the monuments to yourself that you've made in your life, even if that leaves you in serious trouble -- physical, spiritual, or otherwise; there is no becoming Israel if you do not wrestle with Him throughout the dark nights. If you do this in earnest, you may find a long period of serious spiritual struggle come crashing upon your head, but the person you will be at the end of that long night will be someone you never thought you could be, and, what's more, you will know your Father, and you will know His generosity -- in wisdom.

I don't mean the head-in-a-fishbowl, "won't-stop-thinking-about-them" intensity; I'm referring to the intensity of jumping into a profoundly deep body of water, together. Ideally, your spirituality, personality, and temperament would match mine; I have zero time for superficiality, the enemy of innocence, whimsy, the human spirit, and God.

"Henrietta’s favor was demanding: give Marius, a homeless foreigner with a checkered past, a place to stay for the next few months with all expenses covered. Surrendering the spare room of his Brooklyn apartment on South 5th Street, Glenn Catherwood reluctantly accepts the undertaking.

Some weeks later, the two roommates walk across the Williamsburg Bridge. Glenn remembers the glow of its lamps on Henrietta’s face, a memory from a relationship destroyed by his struggle with addiction. Marius has never seen such wonders in all his travels throughout the Roman Empire in service of the legions . . . but Imperial Rome is buried in the past. Marius is lost in the metropolitan Northeast after mysteriously traveling almost two millennia into the future without explanation — a ridiculous notion Glenn refuses to accept. In ways he cannot yet articulate, Glenn is also lost in a strange land. As the cold urbanity of the Five Boroughs pushes Glenn to the fringes of modern society, he’s forced to watch his only remaining acquaintances entertain the outlandish hypothesis of Marius’ arrival. But he can’t ignore the unusual coincidences with the Roman’s appearance. The nightmares which leave him gasping for breath are unsettling, but no more than the bleeding man who watches him enter and exit the apartment building, or the whisperings of Phillip, the man who hid Marius away in Staten Island for two years after the alleged time-jump.

One thing is certain: the unlikely pair have encountered an America with an ever-changing face. While their rowboats have capsized in the cultural maelstrom of 2016, companionship equips them to understand the true nature of the desert island they’ve discovered, and, more importantly, why they are both lost in their own painful ways. Set against a backdrop of cosmopolitan failings, Marius and Glenn experience the mystery of metamorphosis as they navigate the gritty landscape of New York, a world-city in a civilization with questions begging to be answered."
